question: After counting independent predictor-training labels in the total human-label budget, what existence and estimation gains remain relative to direct human-logit fitting?
stage: Finite-sample diagnostic; no efficiency theorem, generic dominance claim, or simulated-human empirical claim
true_logit: intercept zero, first slope 1.5, all other slopes zero; independent standard Gaussian attributes
training_rule: Mean logistic loss plus 0.1/2 times squared norm of all parameters, including the intercept; independent training subset only
label_accounting: Training and correction label subsets are disjoint; their union is exactly the labels used by both all-label comparators. Auxiliary features carry no observed labels.
pairing: Within a condition and repetition all methods share training, correction and auxiliary feature rows and a common independent 4096-row Gaussian integration design. Conditions use independent random-number substreams.
missingness: Retain every planned method row. Report structural nonexistence and numerical unresolved fits separately. Risk averages are conditional on returned verified fits, with paired contrasts reported only on explicitly counted shared fits.
analysis_limits: 100 repetitions provide a diagnostic rather than a precise small-difference ranking
No training-overlap convergence or high-dimensional coverage theorem is inferred
No new human responses or LLM questionnaire responses are generated
No interval-coverage assessment in this experiment
Fixed correction powers are stress-test choices, not new tuned procedures
package_policy: The already verified 245-file reproduction package remains frozen until this separate exploration is reviewed.
